article.title: Before Acting, Know What Is Running
article.subtitle: Runtime context turns process control into evidence-driven engineering.
article.hook: The same command can be safe in one runtime and destructive in another. The control plane needs a live model of the environment before it chooses an action.
article.problem: Static configuration tells us what should be running. Engineering decisions often depend on what is actually running: which process owns a port, which JAR version started, whether a simulator or real dependency is active, what health endpoints report and where logs are flowing. Without runtime context, an automation system may restart the wrong process, diagnose stale logs or test against an unexpected dependency.
article.thesis: Execution decisions should consume live runtime context, not only configuration intent.
article.takeaway: Configuration is intended state. Runtime context is observed state. Safe automation needs both.
article.next_article: Article 5 connects runtime observations with durable engineering knowledge through the Knowledge Spine.

task.title: Diagnose why an API is not responding after a local restart
task.description: The configured profile says the service should listen on one port, but another Java process may still own it and the active logs may belong to a previous run.

journey.name: Read intent
journey.why: Load expected process, artifact, ports and dependencies.

journey.name: Observe processes
journey.why: Inspect PIDs, commands, ports and start times.

journey.name: Probe health
journey.why: Call configured health endpoints and dependency checks.

journey.name: Correlate logs
journey.why: Associate log streams with the active runtime instance.

journey.name: Compare state
journey.why: Identify drift between intended and observed runtime.

journey.name: Choose action
journey.why: Restart, stop, diagnose or refuse based on evidence.

decisions.title: Observed state is versioned context
decisions.body: Runtime discovery should produce a structured snapshot rather than scattered command output. A snapshot can include process identity, artifact checksum, ports, dependency health, environment fingerprint and log pointers.

decisions.title: Drift becomes a decision input
decisions.body: If the active process does not match the profile, the system should surface drift explicitly. The correct next step may be to stop an orphaned process, change the profile or refuse to run a destructive command.

decisions.title: Context has provenance
decisions.body: Every observation should record how and when it was obtained. A port scan, process query, health endpoint and log parser have different reliability. Provenance prevents stale or weak observations from silently becoming facts.

story.evidence_narrative: A runtime context engine should be testable without AI. Given process-list, port and health-probe inputs, it should construct the same normalized snapshot and identify the same drift. AI can later interpret that snapshot, but collection and normalization remain deterministic.

implementation_notes: Collectors gather process, port, health and log metadata through small adapters.
The normalized snapshot separates intended state from observed state.
Drift rules are deterministic and produce reason codes.
Higher-level planning consumes the snapshot rather than raw shell output.

claims.claim: Runtime context distinguishes intended state from observed state
Deterministic drift rules can operate without an LLM
Runtime observations carry timestamp and source provenance
